findings.claim: Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, so descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not final affinity benefit. Survival enrichment (e.g. survival_effects:0 landmark_00_soft_mass z=0.365, q=0.120; survival_effects:100 landmark_10_soft_mass z=0.234, q=0.302) and endpoint contrasts (endpoint_effects:15 landmark_00_occupancy3 integrated z=0.545, q=2.4e-4; endpoint_effects:9 pair_kernel_1.5 z=0.562, q=1.5e-4) disagree in magnitude and multiplicity-adjusted support, so last-record survival credit must not be presented as final affinity benefit. The unavailable terminal-label comparison is reported as unavailable.

Ancestral coverage is thin: lineage_support reports 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, out of 700 batch nodes, and only 14 complete-survival batches. Survival fields are BH-adjusted jointly over 400 tests and are not terminal affinity effects. Immediate selection evidence (endpoint_effects:9-11 pair kernels 1.5/2.5/3.5, q<=9.8e-5, positive_batch_fraction=1.0) is stronger than descendant survival credit (survival_effects:0 q=0.120; survival_effects:100 q=0.302), so direction priorities should weight immediate endpoint contrasts over survival credit.

Multiplicity-adjusted support and independent-batch agreement rank coordinate hypotheses differently from point estimates alone. pair_kernel_1.5 and 2.5 survive both raw and adjusted covariance/correlation with q<=0.081 and same-sign batch fractions 0.79-0.93 (branch_adjusted:86,87,240,241,163,164), while joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are negative with q<=0.030 and same-sign fractions 0.93-1.0 (branch_adjusted:228,230,305,307). A concrete priority decision: rank pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 and joint internal/innovation RMS above global_centroid_x/y/z, whose adjusted CIs cross zero (branch_adjusted:77-79,231-233) despite nonzero raw point estimates.

Independent-batch agreement and opposing observations constrain the joint-motion direction. joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are consistently negative across raw and adjusted covariance/correlation (branch_adjusted:74,76,151,153,228,230,305,307; same-sign batch fractions 0.79-1.0), and joint_diagnostics:2 shows observed_child_score_gain negatively associated with selection innovation (z=-0.036, q=1.8e-7, positive_batch_fraction=0.0). A counterexample that would weaken a proposed direction is any batch where joint_internal_RMS_A increases while child score gain rises; the supplied evidence shows the opposite sign, so the joint-motion direction is retained but only as a coordinate contrast, not a causal selection effect.

Local coordinate information is separated from global pose and shape by the adjusted joint diagnostics. joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A remain negative after adjustment (branch_adjusted:151,153,305,307), while global_centroid_x/y/z adjusted CIs cross zero (branch_adjusted:77-79,231-233). joint_diagnostics:14 reports teacher_contrast_internal_fraction mean 0.787 and joint_diagnostics:1 innovation_native_alignment z=0.092 (q=2.2e-9), indicating internal-motion information beyond common translation/rotation. The extent that should retain freedom is the internal RMS region (joint_internal_RMS_A) and the surrounding landmark local fields; the global centroid and rigid pose should not be treated as informative. No adjustment beyond the supplied adjusted_covariance/adjusted_correlation is claimed.

Coherent joint coordinate patterns are distinguished from isolated marginal descriptors. pair_kernel_1.5 and 2.5 are coupled across raw covariance, adjusted covariance and adjusted correlation (branch_adjusted:86,87,240,241,163,164) with same-sign batch fractions 0.79-0.93, whereas pair_kernel_3.5 and 5.0 lose support after adjustment (branch_adjusted:88,89,242,243; CIs cross zero). joint_diagnostics:4 teacher_contrast_coherence mean 0.812 and joint_diagnostics:14 internal fraction 0.787 indicate coupled internal structure. Incompatible conformations are not averaged into an unsupported target; only the coupled short-range pair kernels are retained.

The supplied continuous contrast functions span observed support [0.0,0.49] with no extrapolation allowed and no accepted polynomial (polynomial_accepted=false throughout). Sign changes are frequent (e.g. continuous:0 landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict; continuous:1 landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts), and relative node RMSE is large (0.29-0.99). curve_support selects only 24 of the audited curves under strict fidelity rules (relative_rmse_le 0.35, strong_sign_conflict_nodes_eq 0, quiet_node_large_fit_fraction_le 0.1). A constant rule is therefore not supported over a time-conditioned rule; the contrast curve is not an absolute reward target.

Rate changes across the observed support are large and sign-inconsistent: first_rate_z and last_rate_z often differ in sign (e.g. continuous:0 first_rate_z=9.27, last_rate_z=-10.00; continuous:1 first_rate_z=-17.49, last_rate_z=8.11), and whole_window_z is small relative to the endpoint rates. This supports a time-conditioned rule over a constant rule, but only within the observed support and only using validated fits or observed-node interpolation; no arbitrary time bins or extrapolation are used.

Population-contrast changes and parent-child increment contrasts are compared with the turnover residual. Population rates are small (turnover:0 landmark_00_soft_mass mean_rate_z=0.185, p=0.72), edge rates are larger (turnover:1 z=4.55, p=0.034), and turnover_residual_rate is negative and comparable in magnitude (turnover:2 z=-4.36, p=0.034). The residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity. The evidence supports changing cohort composition (reclassification and parent weighting) as a substantial component, not within-path change alone.

Within-path change is supported where turnover_residual_rate is positive and significant with high positive_batch_fraction (e.g. turnover:14 landmark_00_local_cxx z=4.29, p=0.002, positive_batch_fraction=0.857; turnover:17 landmark_00_local_cyy z=5.05, p=0.0015, positive_batch_fraction=0.929; turnover:47 landmark_01_local_cyy z=6.40, p=4.3e-4, positive_batch_fraction=0.786). Increment contrasts show the same direction for landmark_00_softmin (increment_effects:14 z=-4.91, q=0.046) and landmark_00_occupancy3 (increment_effects:15 z=4.28, q=0.081). The residual remains an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect.

A testable coordinate intervention is expressible within the permitted reward recipes. Observable: pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 and joint_internal_RMS_A contrasts. Intended response: increased short-range pair-kernel density and reduced joint internal RMS. Target origin: evidence-bound landmark regions (e.g. landmark_00, landmark_01, landmark_02) with verified continuous salience. Spatial scale: pointcloud_delta_A in {0.5,1.0,2.0} A; temporal scale: temporal_region_index with temporal_teacher_blend in {0.25,0.5,1.0} over the observed support [0.0,0.49]. Discriminating failure condition: no change in pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 or joint_internal_RMS_A while global centroid shifts, which would indicate common-motion rather than internal-motion response. The permitted reward recipe that could express this is the temporal_teacher blend with a temporal_region_index; otherwise the finding remains descriptive.

The information audit reports compressed_choice_excess_fixed_RMS_A mean 0.081 (CI 0.070-0.092) and top4_teacher_overlap mean 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515), with teacher score correlations observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor. Teacher modes count 28 with assignment RMS quantiles [0.446,0.863,1.050] A. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit; they do not establish causal affinity benefit or a gradient.

hypotheses.claim: Hypothesis: a pointcloud_delta_A of 1.0 A applied to the evidence-bound landmark_00/landmark_01/landmark_02 regions will increase pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 contrasts without shifting the global centroid. Observable: pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 integrated z. Intended response: positive change in pair_kernel_1.5/2.5. Target origin: landmark_00, landmark_01, landmark_02. Spatial scale: pointcloud_delta_A=1.0 A. Temporal scale: whole window [0.0,0.5]. Discriminating failure condition: global_centroid_x/y/z shifts while pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 does not.

Hypothesis: a temporal_region_index with temporal_teacher_blend=0.5 over the observed support will reduce joint_internal_RMS_A while preserving joint_innovation_RMS_A sign. Observable: joint_internal_RMS_A and joint_innovation_RMS_A. Intended response: negative change in joint_internal_RMS_A. Target origin: evidence-bound landmark with verified continuous salience. Spatial scale: pointcloud_delta_A=1.0 A. Temporal scale: temporal_teacher_blend=0.5. Discriminating failure condition: joint_internal_RMS_A unchanged while joint_translation_RMS_A changes.

Hypothesis: a time-conditioned rule using temporal_teacher_blend=0.25 over the observed support will track the sign changes in the validated continuous curves better than a constant rule. Observable: continuous contrast functions with polynomial_accepted=false and relative_node_RMSE. Intended response: reduced sign conflict between fitted and empirical last-node z. Target origin: evidence-bound landmark with verified continuous salience. Spatial scale: pointcloud_delta_A=1.0 A. Temporal scale: temporal_teacher_blend=0.25. Discriminating failure condition: no reduction in strong_sign_conflict_nodes relative to the constant rule.

Hypothesis: a temporal_region_index targeting landmark_00_local_cxx and landmark_00_local_cyy with temporal_teacher_blend=1.0 will reproduce the positive turnover_residual_rate direction. Observable: turnover_residual_rate and increment_effects. Intended response: positive change in turnover_residual_rate for those features. Target origin: landmark_00. Spatial scale: pointcloud_delta_A=0.5 A. Temporal scale: temporal_teacher_blend=1.0. Discriminating failure condition: turnover_residual_rate sign reverses while population_rate is unchanged.

Hypothesis: a pointcloud_delta_A of 2.0 A applied to the evidence-bound landmark_00 region will increase pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 but not pair_kernel_3.5/5.0, testing the short-range coupling. Observable: pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 versus pair_kernel_3.5/5.0 adjusted contrasts. Intended response: positive change in pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 only. Target origin: landmark_00. Spatial scale: pointcloud_delta_A=2.0 A. Temporal scale: whole window [0.0,0.5]. Discriminating failure condition: pair_kernel_3.5/5.0 changes as much as pair_kernel_1.5/2.5.

Hypothesis: a temporal_region_index with temporal_teacher_blend=0.5 and pointcloud_delta_A=0.5 A will reduce joint_internal_RMS_A more than joint_translation_RMS_A. Observable: joint_internal_RMS_A versus joint_translation_RMS_A. Intended response: larger negative change in joint_internal_RMS_A. Target origin: evidence-bound landmark with verified continuous salience. Spatial scale: pointcloud_delta_A=0.5 A. Temporal scale: temporal_teacher_blend=0.5. Discriminating failure condition: joint_translation_RMS_A changes more than joint_internal_RMS_A.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles
Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, so last-record credit is not presented as final affinity benefit
Teacher score correlations are observational and are not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor
Moment effects, pair kernels and turnover rates are diagnostic evidence only; the executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term
